column1: [Kernel Modules] Which command displays all currently active and inserted kernel modules on a running system?
[Kernel Modules] What is the difference between insmod and modprobe when inserting a kernel module?
column2: modprobe automatically resolves and loads module dependencies and requires only the module name, while insmod requires the full file path and does not handle dependencies.

column1: [Kernel Modules] Which command is used to remove a currently loaded module from the running Linux kernel?
[Kernel Modules] How does modprobe differ from rmmod when unloading kernel modules?
column2: modprobe -r removes the specified module along with its unused dependencies, whereas rmmod only removes the specified module.
